description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Diarrhoea history structure
points: Acute (<2 weeks, usually infectious) vs chronic (>4 weeks, broader differential including IBD/malabsorption) is the key first branch.
Blood/mucus, nocturnal symptoms, and weight loss point away from simple functional diarrhoea toward an organic cause.
Travel, food exposure, and recent antibiotics are essential for the infectious/C. difficile differential.

modules.title: Diarrhoea alarm features
points: Nocturnal diarrhoea, blood/mucus, weight loss, or dehydration are alarm features that separate organic disease (e.g. IBD) from functional causes.
Significant dehydration or systemic toxicity warrants urgent fluid resuscitation.

Q000091.why_ask: Duration beyond a few weeks reframes the differential toward chronic/organic causes such as IBD.
Q000091.think: Chronic bloody diarrhoea with weight loss should prompt colonoscopic evaluation.

Q000051.why_ask: Diarrhoea that wakes the patient from sleep is a classic organic (non-functional) red flag.
listen_for: Wakes from sleep vs only during the day
Q000051.think: Nocturnal symptoms are rarely explained by irritable bowel syndrome alone.

Q000052.why_ask: Recent antibiotic exposure raises concern for C. difficile-associated diarrhoea.
Q000052.think: This should prompt stool testing for C. difficile toxin when clinically appropriate.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: nocturnal diarrhoea
points: Organic cause more likely than functional (e.g. IBS).
Prioritise inflammatory markers and consider colonoscopy.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: chronic course
